newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: IGB, Ipmuda shares to remain suspended - KLSE.
newsitem.headline: IGB, Ipmuda shares to remain suspended - KLSE.

text.p: Trading in the shares of IGB Corp Bhd and Ipmuda Bhd will remain suspended until further notice, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Saturday.
"The Committee of the Exchange has decided that suspension of the companies be maintained until further notice," the KLSE said in a circular to members. It gave no further details.
Exchange officials could not be reached for comment.
On Thursday, IGB Corp announced that it has received an offer from Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd to buy a controlling 32.9 percent stake in IGB unit Ipmuda for 160.27 million ringgit in cash.
IGB said the offer is being considered by its board.

The offer would consist of 23.03 million Ipmuda shares at 5.50 ringgit a share for 126.67 million ringgit and 11.2 million Ipmuda warrants at 3.00 ringgit per warrant for 33.6 million ringgit in cash.
IGB and Ipmuda also requested the suspension in their stocks be lifted. IGB's stock closed at 2.93 ringgit on February 4, while Ipmuda ended at 6.20 ringgit on January 28.
Ipmuda is involved in trading and making building materials. IGB's activities include property development, construction management services. Maju Holdings is a privately-held steel concern.
